item.text:
This pass widened and quantified Finding 1, and added a labeled secondary suspicion. Report updated at [report.md](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-08_13-11-14-hashicorp_raft-baseline/work/report.md).

**New executed evidence**

- Flakiness campaign over exactly the 10 `EnsureSamePeers` callers (`-count=10`, `audit/campaign.log`): **3 failures in 120 executions** — `TestRaft_HasExistingState` 1/10 and `TestRaft_ProtocolVersion_Upgrade_1_2` 2/10; the other eight callers were clean in this sample. The failure signature is always `testing.go:705 peer mismatch`, with the stale `peerSet` being the older/smaller configuration.
- Fix-verification diagnostic (`TestAudit_EnsureSamePeers_Fixed`, `-count=20`, `audit/audit-fixed.log`): **20/20 pass, 0 failures** with a single re-read of the reference configuration each pass — closing the loop that the cached `peerSet` is the entire cause and the one-line change resolves it for all 10 callers.
- Prior pass this session: full non-network suite under `-race` is clean (0 data races), so no concurrency defect was surfaced in the exercised paths.

**Secondary, clearly-labeled suspicion (not executed)**

`(*cluster).EnsureLeader` (`testing.go:582-604`) is the only one of the three helper assertions with **no retry/timeout** — it does one `LeaderWithID()` comparison and fails immediately. `EnsureSamePeers` waits for *configuration* agreement, not *leader* agreement, so a configuration change could leave `EnsureLeader` exposed to the same class of spurious failure. I record this as source-based only; I did not observe it failing.

No defect was found in the core consensus/agreement logic, and the artifact remains byte-identical to upstream v1.7.3. `source/` is untouched; additions are confined to `audit/`, `audit_diag_test.go`, and `report.md`.
